questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

After we had ate a hearty meal, we went to sleep
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'After we had ate'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'After we had eaten'** should be used instead of **'After we had ate'.**
 
• We know that after '**had**' **past participle** is used.
 
• In the given sentence past participle of '**eat**' is '**eaten**'.
 
• When two things happen one after the other in the past, then past perfect tense is used with the first incident, and in the clause of the second incident, we use simple past tense. 
 
 
• *Example: She **asked **me if I **had eaten**.*

 
 
 

**Correct Sentence:__** *After we **had eaten** a hearty meal, we went to sleep.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

• यहाँ,** 'After we had ate'** के स्थान पर** 'After we had eaten' **का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• हम जानते हैं कि '**had**' के बाद **past participle** का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
 
• जब एक के बाद एक चीजें होती हैं, तो पहली घटना के साथ** Past Perfect Tense** का इस्तेमाल होता है और दूसरी घटना के **clause** में हम **Simple Past Tense **का इस्तेमाल करते हैं।

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’**

Please don’t create panic among people during __that__ difficult times.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**these**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, '**these**' should be used instead of '**that**'.
 
• **This, that, these, and those** are **demonstratives**. We use **this, that, these, and those** to point to people and things.** ****This** and **that** are singular.
 
• '**These**' refers to** plural nouns** (i.e. these cookies).
 
• Generally speaking, we use this/these to refer to people and things, situations, and experiences that are close to the speaker or very close in time.
 
• In the given sentence '**difficult times**' is plural and refers to the near situation. Hence, '**these**' should be used.

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Please don't create panic among people during **these **difficult times.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहाँ '**that**' के स्थान पर '**these**' का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
 
• **This, that, these**, और **those** **demonstratives** हैं। हम इस this, that, these, and those का उपयोग लोगों और चीजों को इंगित करने के लिए करते हैं। This और **that** एकवचन हैं।
 
• '**These**' **plural nouns** (**i.e. these cookies**) को संदर्भित करता है।
 
• आम तौर पर, हम इसका उपयोग लोगों और चीजों, स्थितियों और अनुभवों को संदर्भित करने के लिए करते हैं जो स्पीकर के करीब हैं या समय के बहुत करीब हैं।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में **'difficult times'** बहुवचन है और निकट स्थिति को दर्शाता है। इसलिए '**these**' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।

questions.question: Let x be the largest 4-digit number which is divisible by each of 16, 21, 24 and 28. The sum of the digits of X is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **LCM** of 16, 21, 24, and 28 is **336**.

Largest 4-digit number 9999 ÷ 336 leaves a **remainder** of 255.

Largest 4-digit multiple (x) = 9999 − 255 = **9744**.

Sum of digits of 9744 = 9 + 7 + 4 + 4 = **24**.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors are **16, 21, 24, and 28**.

**Formula Used:** x = **Largest 4-digit number** − (Largest 4-digit number mod **LCM** of divisors).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/406e0f2c341db863f0eb7fe0181043ba2c485c362f8fb07382fd403899bee673.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization of 16 = 2⁴

⇒ Prime factorization of 21 = 3 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ **LCM** = 2⁴ × 3 × 7 = 16 × 21 = **336**

⇒ **Largest 4-digit number** = 9999

⇒ 9999 ÷ 336 ⇒ Quotient = 29, Remainder = 255

⇒ Required number **x** = 9999 − 255 = **9744**

⇒ **Sum of digits** = 9 + 7 + 4 + 4 = **24**

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** is the smallest positive integer that is exactly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is calculated by taking the highest power of each prime factor involved.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by **3** if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3. Since 9744 is a multiple of 21 and 24, it must be divisible by 3.

Division Algorithm

For any dividend and divisor: **Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder**. To find the largest multiple below a limit, subtract the remainder from that limit.</p

questions.question: Which of the following parallels of latitude represent the Tropic of Capricorn?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23 1/2o in the Southern Hemisphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **23 1/2o **____**in the Southern Hemisphere parallels of latitude represent the Tropic of Capricorn**__.
 
• The **Tropic of Capricorn **(or the Southern Tropic) is the circle of latitude that contains the subsolar point at the December (or southern) solstice.

 [IMAGE: https://media.istockphoto.com/illustrations/antique-illustration-1978-geography-outline-of-the-tropics-and-polar-illustration-id1174207942?k=20&m=1174207942&s=612x612&w=0&h=08AD_lDSPy0K6p16luaivQF9_aMx4VVJ0zIfTlWpE-8=] 

__
 
• It is thus the southernmost latitude where the Sun can be seen directly overhead.
 
• It also reaches 90 degrees below the horizon at solar midnight on the June Solstice.
 
• Its northern equivalent is the Tropic of Cancer.
 
• The Tropic of Capricorn is one of the five major circles of latitude marked on maps of Earth.
 
• Its latitude is currently **23°26′11.1″ (or 23.43641°)** south of the Equator, but it is very gradually moving northward, currently at the rate of 0.47 arcseconds, or 15 meters, per year.
 
• Less than** 3%** of the world's population lives south of it; this is equivalent to about 30% of the population of the Southern Hemisphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **latitude **is the angle formed by a line going from the center of the earth to the equator at the point on the equator that is closed to the point of interest and another line that goes from the center of the earth to the parallel that goes through the point of interest.

 
 
• Latitude is a measurement on a globe or map of location north or south of the Equator.
 
• Lines joining places with the same latitudes are called parallels ie the lines running East to West are called “Parallels” or “lines of latitude”.
 
• Technically, there are different kinds of latitude—geocentric, astronomical, and geographic (or geodetic)—but there are only minor differences between them.
 
• In most common references, geocentric latitude is implied.
 
• Given in degrees, minutes, and seconds, geocentric latitude is the arc subtended by an angle at Earth’s centre and measured in a north-south plane poleward from the Equator.
 
• Therefore, the greatest possible latitudes are** 90° N and 90° S**.
 
 
 
• **Important parallels of latitude**:
 
 
• The equator
 
• The Tropic of Cancer (23½ºN)
 
• The Tropic of Capricorn (23½ºS)
 
• The Arctic Circle (66½ºN)
 
• The Antarctic Circle (66½ºS)
